fixes.explanation: Fear is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't the word in this verse. The text says, "Thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him." (Judges 10:6) The same verse says they served the Baals, the Ashtoreths and the gods of the nations around them. The word you want is forsook, as in left Him behind.

Praise is a lovely word, friend, but it isn't the one this verse uses. The text says, "Thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him." (Judges 10:6) It says the Israelites served the Baals, the Ashtoreths and other gods. Forsook is the word, and it means they left Him.

Those two are real nations, so I see why they came to mind. The Midianites show up earlier in Judges (Judges 6:1), but not here. In this passage the text says the LORD "…sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites…" (Judges 10:7) Keep those two names handy, because you'll hear them again.

Now those are some old names, friend. The Hittites and Jebusites are both on the list of peoples in the land (Exodus 3:8). But in this passage the text says the LORD "…sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites…" (Judges 10:7) Different crowd this time.

Forty is a big number in the Bible, so I get the pull. But the text here says the Philistines and Ammonites "…harassed and oppressed the Israelites, and they did so for eighteen years…" (Judges 10:8) That's a long stretch, but not forty.

Showing up with a gift is a classic move, but that's not what the text says here. It says, "Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD…" (Judges 10:10) A confession came with that cry, because they said they had sinned against Him. They came with words, not presents.

False is right, baker. Listen to the question the LORD asks: "…you cried out to Me, did I not save you from their hands?" (Judges 10:12) He's looking back at the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians, Amalekites and Maonites. When Israel cried out then, the answer was a rescue, not a leave-behind.

More time is the opposite of what they asked for, friend. What they say is, "Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!" (Judges 10:15) They wanted deliverance, and they wanted it today. Not later.

A king would be a big ask, friend, but that's not what they say to the LORD here. They say, "Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!" (Judges 10:15) Their request was to be delivered, and the word "today" is right in it.

Marching into battle with those gods would be a bold plan, but the text doesn't say that. It says, "So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD…" (Judges 10:16) The foreign gods were put away, and they served the LORD.

True. After they put away the foreign gods and served the LORD, "…He could no longer bear the misery of Israel." (Judges 10:16) That's a tender line, and I think it's worth reading twice. The text puts the LORD's response right after their turn back to Him.

That's what they say. The rulers of Gilead tell one another, "Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all who live in Gilead." (Judges 10:18) The verse before says the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites camped at Mizpah. So the offer is leadership for whoever steps up first.
